investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a legal actor schedule lets the origin process the new ballot and the decided advance to idx before any drain_notifiers pass observes the stale pending (the false Ok is avoided if a tick drains while decided < idx, yielding Superseded), and whether the decided entry at idx is the replacement rather than the caller's entry.

investigations.question: When a DecidedSub starts below the compacted index, does its per-element cursor arithmetic stay index-aligned with read_decided_suffix, or does it re-deliver already-emitted entries on later pushes?

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.

knowledge.statement: Pending append_notify calls in the runtime actor are resolved in this order: Ok(idx) when the recorded assignment index is <= the actor's current decided index; Superseded when the assignment ballot is lower than the current promise ballot; Timeout when the deadline passed; otherwise the pending stays queued. The Ok arm is evaluated first and does not inspect the log or compare the entry stored at idx.

knowledge.statement: create_log_sync sends the StopSign in a separate log_sync field and starts the suffix at the follower's valid entries index, then sync_log sets accepted_idx to sync_idx + suffix length and adds one more when log_sync carries a StopSign. Since nothing may be appended after an accepted StopSign, decided can reach at most that last position and stopsign_is_decided (decided == accepted) can never become true for that follower. knowledge.statement: append on a non-leader creates one ProposalForward message addressed to the current leader and moves the entries into it; the core keeps no copy for retry. resend_messages_follower resends only the cached Promise (Prepare phase) or PrepareReq (Recover), and resend_messages_leader resends Prepare, AcceptStopSign and the StopSign's Decide. A ProposalForward lost in transport, or received by a leader that fails before accepting it, is therefore not re-proposed by the core; the caller's transport and any application-level retry carry that duty. The runtime layer's TaggedProposal path does retry undispatched proposals on ticks, which is a separate, stronger contract.

knowledge.statement: When the outgoing channel does not accept a message, messages accumulate in outgoing_buf; once its length exceeds the channel capacity (or max_outgoing_buffered), drain_outgoing_buf drops the oldest entries before retrying. The same buffer holds core protocol traffic pulled by flush_outgoing, including PaxosMsg::ProposalForward produced when a plain append is issued on a follower, and runtime control messages enqueued by try_dispatch_undispatched (TaggedProposal) and by Assigned replies. Core resends Promise/PrepareReq/Prepare/AcceptStopSign/StopSign-Decide but not ProposalForward, and the runtime does not resend TaggedProposal, so dropping those messages loses the corresponding client proposal (a tagged proposal then resolves only by timeout; a plain forwarded append is not retried at all). The configuration docs justify drop-oldest as safe because OmniPaxos tolerates lost messages, which covers protocol messages but not these client-origin ones.
knowledge.conditions: Runtime actor with outgoing channel backpressure sustained long enough for outgoing_buf to exceed its cap while client-origin messages are queued; the caller is expected to drain outgoing_messages continuously, so sustained non-draining is a caller-duty violation and bounds the applicability.

knowledge.statement: handle_majority_promises applies exactly one promise log_sync, the one kept as max_promise_sync while promises are collected in the Prepare phase. handle_promise_accept, the path for a Promise that arrives once the leader is already in the Accept phase, only records the promise metadata and sends that follower an AcceptSync; it never merges the Promise's log_sync into the leader's storage. A follower that accepted a StopSign and then promises after the prepare quorum therefore does not give the leader that StopSign, even though it is part of an accept quorum at the StopSign's index and reports that index in later Accepted replies, which is_chosen counts toward the leader's decision.

knowledge.statement: set_promise keeps only the log_sync of the greatest PromiseMetaData seen while promises are collected, and PromiseMetaData compares by n_accepted first and accepted_idx second. handle_majority_promises then applies that single log_sync. investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.

knowledge.statement: create_log_sync sends the StopSign in a separate log_sync field and starts the suffix at the follower's valid entries index, then sync_log sets accepted_idx to sync_idx + suffix length and adds one more when log_sync carries a StopSign. knowledge.statement: append on a non-leader creates one ProposalForward message addressed to the current leader and moves the entries into it; the core keeps no copy for retry. resend_messages_follower resends only the cached Promise (Prepare phase) or PrepareReq (Recover), and resend_messages_leader resends Prepare, AcceptStopSign and the StopSign's Decide. A ProposalForward lost in transport, or received by a leader that fails before accepting it, is therefore not re-proposed by the core; the caller's transport and any application-level retry carry that duty. The runtime layer's TaggedProposal path does retry undispatched proposals on ticks, which is a separate, stronger contract.

knowledge.statement: When the outgoing channel does not accept a message, messages accumulate in outgoing_buf; once its length exceeds the channel capacity (or max_outgoing_buffered), drain_outgoing_buf drops the oldest entries before retrying. The same buffer holds core protocol traffic pulled by flush_outgoing, including PaxosMsg::ProposalForward produced when a plain append is issued on a follower, and runtime control messages enqueued by try_dispatch_undispatched (TaggedProposal) and by Assigned replies. Core resends Promise/PrepareReq/Prepare/AcceptStopSign/StopSign-Decide but not ProposalForward, and the runtime does not resend TaggedProposal, so dropping those messages loses the corresponding client proposal (a tagged proposal then resolves only by timeout; a plain forwarded append is not retried at all). The configuration docs justify drop-oldest as safe because OmniPaxos tolerates lost messages, which covers protocol messages but not these client-origin ones.

No AcceptStopSign reached node 5 in that window. Because the leader only sends Prepare to a not-promised peer or in response to a PrepareReq, the unchanged Decide is read as a sequence break that made node 5 reconnect; the AcceptSync then repaired it. This shows the resend path can repair a missing AcceptStopSign when the resend is sequence-ahead of the follower.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; election_tick_timeout 1000 and resend_message_tick_timeout 100; entries 1..2 decided everywhere, then a reconfigure whose AcceptStopSign and first Decide addressed to pid 5 are discarded, followed by 150 tick-driven rounds with all messages delivered and every message to pid 5 delivered individually.

knowledge.statement: handle_accepted advances a leader's decided index to a follower-reported accepted index when that index exceeds the current decided index and is_chosen counts an accept quorum at or beyond it. is_chosen counts entries in accepted_indexes, which mixes the leader's own accepted index with follower indices reported in Accepted messages, and never inspects the log, so a leader can decide an index it has not locally accepted, including a StopSign accepted only by followers outside its prepare quorum. Because create_log_sync attaches only the leader's local StopSign, an AcceptSync issued by such a leader carries no StopSign, and resend_messages_leader's StopSign branch is guarded by get_stopsign(), so that leader sends neither AcceptStopSign nor the StopSign's Decide for the missing position.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos leader in Phase::Accept; a quorum of accepted_indexes reaches the reported index through the leader's own accepted index plus Accepted messages carrying the leader's ballot; the leader's prepare quorum did not merge a log_sync containing the StopSign, so its local log ends one position before the StopSign; no snapshots involved.

knowledge.statement: handle_majority_promises applies exactly one promise log_sync, the one kept as max_promise_sync while promises are collected in the Prepare phase. handle_promise_accept, the path for a Promise that arrives once the leader is already in the Accept phase, only records the promise metadata and sends that follower an AcceptSync; it never merges the Promise's log_sync into the leader's storage. A follower that accepted a StopSign and then promises after the prepare quorum therefore does not give the leader that StopSign, even though it is part of an accept quorum at the StopSign's index and reports that index in later Accepted replies, which is_chosen counts toward the leader's decision.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos leader that reached a prepare quorum without any log_sync containing the StopSign; the StopSign-holding follower's Promise arrives after the leader switched to Phase::Accept; no snapshots involved.

knowledge.statement: set_promise keeps only the log_sync of the greatest PromiseMetaData seen while promises are collected, and PromiseMetaData compares by n_accepted first and accepted_idx second. handle_majority_promises then applies that single log_sync. A follower whose Promise carries a later accept round but a shorter log is therefore greater than a follower whose Promise carries an earlier round and a longer log including an accepted StopSign, and the longer log's StopSign is never merged into the leader. The leader can hold a prepare quorum that intersects the StopSign holders and still reach Phase::Accept without the StopSign, which also means resend_messages_leader's StopSign branch, guarded by get_stopsign(), stays inactive for that position.
knowledge.conditions: SequencePaxos leader collecting promises in Phase::Prepare; at least two promises differ in n_accepted or accepted_idx so only one wins the max comparison; the losing promise's log_sync is the only one containing the StopSign; no snapshots involved.

knowledge.statement: In convergence round 3 of the seeded run 13, the four Promises delivered to node 4 carried ballot n=2 and read: from1 na1 aidx37 didx0 ss1, from2 na1 aidx37 didx0 ss1, from3 na0 aidx0 didx0 ss0, from5 na1 aidx37 didx0 ss1. Node 4's accepted index changed from 0 to 37 in that same round and stayed 37, while its decided index ended at 38. No Promise addressed to node 4 was delivered during the earlier 900 randomized actions.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c, reconfigure at action 450 with 20 percent out-of-order loss, then 150 fair-delivery rounds; Promises are recorded only when actually delivered to pid 4 and only the first forty are kept, and node 4's accepted index is sampled after each convergence round.

knowledge.statement: At the end of the seeded run 13, node 3 reports is_reconfigured Some with accepted 37 and decided 37, while node 4 reports is_reconfigured None with accepted 37 and decided 38. Node 3 received Decides with sequence counters 2 and 3 after its AcceptSync with counter 1 and both left its decided index at 37, while node 4's decided index is 38. In convergence round 3 node 4 received StopSign-bearing Promises from nodes 1, 2 and 5 at accept round 1 and accepted index 37, and its own accepted index rose from 0 to 37 in that round.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c, reconfigure at action 450 with 20 percent out-of-order loss, then 150 fair-delivery rounds; is_reconfigured is sampled once at the end and Promises only when delivered to pid 4.

knowledge.statement: sync_log replaces the local StopSign when the applied log_sync carries one, and when the applied log_sync carries none while the node already has a stored StopSign it clears that StopSign and records a SetStopsign(None) operation. The clearing branch runs for any sync_log caller, so an AcceptSync built from a leader or peer whose log lacks the StopSign erases the marker on a node that had already accepted it, independently of the accepted-index arithmetic.
knowledge.conditions: A node with an accepted StopSign applies a LogSync whose stopsign field is None, through sync_log; no snapshots are involved and the sync's suffix need not be empty.

knowledge.statement: In receipt 603faa15c86645c6a56b0b9fadfc0751, node 5 reported is_reconfigured Some with decided 5 at the ready event and is_reconfigured None with decided 4 at the after_sync event, after applying an AcceptSync built by a leader whose log had a lower decided index and no StopSign for that position. The transition is the executed instance of sync_log's clearing branch: an applied LogSync with stopsign None removes a locally stored StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; entries 1..4 decided everywhere, a reconfigure whose StopSign is decided only on node 5, node 1 cut, node 2 elected at decided 4, node 5's Prepare lost and reconnected(2) driving PrepareReq/Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync.
